highlight.text: Mountains had long been seen as sacred places in China, which were viewed as the homes of immortals and thus, close to the heavens.

source.label: Edwards, The Field of Stones: the long, learned poem packed into the upper right-hand corner

work.text: [Shen Zhou imitated Wang Meng] because he wished to convey ideas of enduring life and to transmit them to an old and respected teacher that he, like the mountains, might live forever.

source.author: Richard Edwards
source.title: The Field of Stones: A Study of the Art of Shen Chou (1427–1509)

work.text: In contrast to the relatively spare style of his compatriots, his ropy brushstrokes piled one on the other to produce masses of texture combined in dense and involved patterns.
work.lead: On Wang Meng, the Yuan master whose manner Shen Zhou borrowed here:

moment.text: Mount Lu contains important sites and temples for Daoism, (Mahayana) Buddhism, Confucianism, and even Christianity.
The Song dynasty poet Su Shi famously described the difficulty of conveying the mountain's beauty in his expression, "Why can't I tell the true shape of Lushan? Because I myself am in the mountain."

matters.text: On the fifth day of the fifth month, 1467, the pupil, Shen Chou of Suchou, respectfully composed poem and painting, wishing long life for (Ch‘en) Hsing-an
matters.lead: Shen Zhou’s dedication to his old teacher Chen Kuan:

source.author: Shen Zhou (Shen Chou)
source.title: Inscription on Towering Mount Lu, 1467
source.publisher: translated by Richard Edwards in The Field of Stones (Freer Gallery of Art, 1962; Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: I was one who loitered about his door; / Looking up at his lofty eminence / Mount Lu is no longer high. … Fame and wealth to him are like the passing cloud

source.author: Shen Zhou (Shen Chou)
source.title: Poem inscribed on Towering Mount Lu, 1467
source.publisher: translated by Richard Edwards in The Field of Stones (Freer Gallery of Art, 1962; Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: As a result, we should look on the mountain as a kind of portrait of Ch‘en K‘uan.
